findings.title: Crash when Google Meet is selected and no destination calendar exists
findings.body: `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is `undefined` whenever `evt.destinationCalendar` is null or an empty array. Several call sites in this PR now pass `[]`. The code then reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining. For any Google Meet booking where the organizer has no destination calendar, this throws a TypeError. Before this change the access used `?.` and the event fell back to Cal Video; now booking creation fails instead.

findings.title: Video references no longer get a credentialId
findings.body: The reference `credentialId` is now `isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined`, so video results (Zoom, Daily, etc.) are stored with no credentialId. Previously they received `result.credentialId`. `handleCancelBooking` only deletes a video meeting when `bookingVideoReference.credentialId` is set, so cancelling these bookings will leave the external video meetings in place. Credential-based lookup for video updates breaks the same way.

findings.title: Org slug assignment condition inverted (unrelated change)
findings.body: The old code was `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })`, which set the slug only when team billing was disabled. The new code is `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}`, which reverses that. With billing enabled, the slug is now claimed before payment. With billing disabled, organizations are created with no slug at all. This change has nothing to do with destination calendars.

findings.title: Collective hosts' Outlook events go to the first host's calendar id
findings.body: `createEvent` now always uses `destinationCalendar[0]`, the main host's calendar. In a collective event it is called once per host credential. For every other host, it calls `/me/calendars/{mainHostCalendarId}/events` with their own token, which returns 404 or writes to the wrong calendar. It should pick the entry whose `credentialId` matches the credential being used, as the Google service does. Lark (lines 128/164) and the CalDAV `BaseCalendarService.createEvent` (line 156) have the same problem. In the CalDAV case, filtering by the main host's externalId matches none of the other host's calendars, so no event is created and no error is reported.

findings.title: Fallback calendar lookup is dead code; update/delete lose the destination-calendar fallback
findings.body: `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` only reaches `find` when `externalCalendarId` is falsy. In that case it compares against null/undefined and always returns undefined. References with no `externalCalendarId`, such as older bookings, previously fell back to `destinationCalendar.externalId`. Now `updateEvent` passes `calendarId: undefined` and the update fails, while `deleteEvent` targets `primary` and may hit the wrong calendar. The same pattern appears at line 315.

findings.title: Hangout patch uses undefined calendarId when insert used 'primary'
findings.body: The insert call uses `selectedCalendar || "primary"`, but the follow-up `events.patch` passes `selectedCalendar` directly. When no destination calendar matches the credential, that value is undefined. The patch then fails, and the Meet link is never added to the event description.

findings.title: Team members' destination calendars dropped when organizer has none
findings.body: `evt.destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar. In that case `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` does nothing. The other collective hosts' calendars are silently discarded, which is the exact scenario this PR is meant to fix. Initialise the array (for example to `[]`) before pushing.

findings.title: loadUsers drops organization select and masks errors as 500
findings.body: The dynamic-user query no longer selects `organization: { slug }`. Any downstream code that reads `user.organization` for org-aware booker URLs will now see it as undefined. Separately, the new try/catch rethrows every non-Prisma error as a generic 500 "Unable to load users". That includes the explicit dynamicUserList validation error, so what is really a 400 client error comes back as a 500 and its message is lost.

findings.title: Recurring cancellation deletion repeated per reference and misses non-first refs
findings.body: The recurring branch is now inside the loop over calendar references. For each reference with a credential, it again deletes events across all of the organizer's calendar credentials and all updated bookings. With N calendar references this runs N times, sending duplicate delete calls. It also only deletes `updBooking.references.find(...)`, the first calendar reference of each occurrence. Collective hosts' events in later references are never removed, and they are deleted with the organizer's credentials rather than the matching ones.

findings.title: Only first old calendar event deleted when merging on reschedule
findings.body: `updateAllCalendarEvents` now handles multiple calendar references. However, the `newBookingId` merge path still deletes only `booking.references.find(...)`, the first calendar reference. For collective bookings, the other hosts' old calendar events are left behind, producing duplicate events after a seated reschedule.

findings.title: Webhook payload shape of destinationCalendar changed
findings.body: Webhook payloads spread `evt`, so `destinationCalendar` changes from a single object or null to an array. Depending on the trigger it is now `null` or `[]`, as the inconsistent test expectations show. This breaks existing webhook consumers that read `payload.destinationCalendar.externalId`. The change is undocumented and should be called out or versioned.
